```
1	# GitHub API — Available Data
2	
3	Full reference of data extractable from GitHub REST + GraphQL APIs for developer performance tracking.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Commits
8	
9	### Per Commit (single-commit endpoint only)
10	- `sha`, `message` (subject + body), `authored_at`, `committed_at`
11	- `author` + `committer` (may differ on rebase/cherry-pick)
12	- `stats.additions`, `stats.deletions`, `stats.total`
13	- `parents[]` — count > 1 = merge commit
14	- `verification.verified` — GPG/SSH signed
15	- `comment_count`
16	- Per file: `filename`, `status` (added/removed/modified/renamed/copied), `additions`, `deletions`, `patch`
17	
18	### Aggregate Stats (cached, repo-level)
19	- **`/stats/contributors`** — per contributor per week: `additions`, `deletions`, `commits` (52 weeks)
20	- **`/stats/commit_activity`** — per week total + per day of week (52 weeks)
21	- **`/stats/code_frequency`** — weekly additions/deletions since repo creation
22	- **`/stats/participation`** — last 52 weeks: all vs. owner commits
23	- **`/stats/punch_card`** — hourly distribution by day of week — work pattern analysis
24	
25	> **Note**: `additions`/`deletions` require N+1 calls on list endpoints. Use stats endpoints for aggregates.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Pull Requests
30	
31	### Core Fields
32	- `number`, `title`, `body`, `state` (open/closed), `draft`, `merged`, `locked`
33	- `created_at`, `updated_at`, `closed_at`, `merged_at` — **cycle time foundation**
34	- `additions`, `deletions`, `changed_files`, `commits` — PR size
35	- `review_comments` — inline review comments count
36	- `comments` — general comments count
37	- `merge_commit_sha`, `merged_by`
38	- `merge_method` — `merge`, `squash`, `rebase`
39	- `auto_merge` — enabled_by, method, commit config
40	- `author_association` — OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR/CONTRIBUTOR/FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR/FIRST_TIMER
41	- `requested_reviewers[]`, `requested_teams[]`
42	- `assignees[]`, `labels[]`, `milestone`
43	- `mergeable`, `mergeable_state`, `rebaseable`
44	- `maintainer_can_modify`
45	
46	### GraphQL-Only PR Fields
47	- `reviewDecision` — APPROVED / CHANGES_REQUESTED / REVIEW_REQUIRED
48	- `reviewThreads` — each thread: `isResolved`, `isOutdated`, `path`, `line`, `resolvedBy`
49	- `timelineItems` — full ordered event stream (labels, assignments, reviews, commits, status changes)
50	- `closingIssuesReferences` — issues that close on merge
51	- `participants` — all users who touched the PR
52	- `suggestedReviewers` — ML-recommended reviewers
53	- `isInMergeQueue`, `isCrossRepository` (fork PR)
54	- `totalCommentsCount` — combined count
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Code Reviews
59	
60	### Review Object
61	- `state` — APPROVED / CHANGES_REQUESTED / COMMENTED / PENDING / DISMISSED
62	- `submitted_at` — **time-to-review foundation**
63	- `reviewer` (user), `author_association`
64	- `commit_id` — which commit was reviewed
65	
66	### Review Comments (Inline)
67	- `path`, `line`, `original_line`, `side` (LEFT/RIGHT)
68	- `diff_hunk` — surrounding code context
69	- `body`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
70	- `in_reply_to_id` — thread structure
71	- `reactions` — 👍 👎 😄 😕 ❤️ 🎉 👀 🚀
72	- `resolved` (boolean)
73	
74	### GraphQL Review Thread Detail
75	- `isResolved`, `resolvedBy`, `isOutdated`, `isCollapsed`
76	- `path`, `line`, `startLine`, `diffSide`
77	
78	---
79	
80	## Issues
81	
82	### Core Fields
83	- `number`, `title`, `body`, `state` (open/closed)
84	- `state_reason` — completed / reopened / not_planned / duplicate
85	- `created_at`, `updated_at`, `closed_at`, `closed_by`
86	- `assignees[]`, `labels[]`, `milestone`
87	- `comments` count
88	- `reactions` — full rollup
89	- `author_association`
90	- `parent_issue_url`, `sub_issues_summary` (total/completed/percent)
91	- `issue_dependencies_summary` (blocked_by/blocking counts)
92	- `pull_request.merged_at` — present if issue linked to a PR
93	
94	### Timeline Events (per issue)
95	All state changes tracked: labeled/unlabeled, assigned/unassigned, milestoned, renamed, closed/reopened, locked, referenced, cross-referenced, review_requested, reviewed, committed, state_change, added_to_project, moved_column_in_project
96

98	
99	## Repository Statistics & Traffic
100	
101	### Contributor Stats (`/stats/contributors`)
102	Per contributor, per week for 52 weeks: `additions`, `deletions`, `commits`
103	
104	### Traffic (14-day window, requires push access)
105	- `/traffic/views` — total + unique views per day
106	- `/traffic/clones` — total + unique clones per day
107	- `/traffic/popular/referrers` — top 10 referrers
108	- `/traffic/popular/paths` — top 10 popular paths
109	
110	### Repository Fields
111	- `size`, `stargazers_count`, `forks_count`, `watchers_count`, `open_issues_count`
112	- `language` (primary), `topics[]`
113	- `allow_merge_commit`, `allow_squash_merge`, `allow_rebase_merge`, `allow_auto_merge`, `delete_branch_on_merge`
114	- `security_and_analysis` — advanced security, secret scanning status
115	- `web_commit_signoff_required`
116	- Languages breakdown: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages` → bytes per language

120	## GitHub Actions / CI
121	
122	### Workflow Runs
123	- `status` — queued/in_progress/completed/waiting/requested/pending
124	- `conclusion` — success/failure/cancelled/neutral/skipped/timed_out/action_required
125	- `event` — push/pull_request/schedule/workflow_dispatch/release/etc.
126	- `created_at`, `run_started_at`, `updated_at` — queue time = `run_started_at - created_at`
127	- `actor`, `triggering_actor`
128	- `head_sha`, `head_branch`, `workflow_id`
129	- `/timing` endpoint: `run_duration_ms`, `billable.{OS}.total_ms` per job
130	
131	### Workflow Jobs
132	- `name`, `status`, `conclusion`
133	- `created_at`, `started_at`, `completed_at` — job duration
134	- `runner_name`, `runner_group_name`, `labels[]`
135	- `steps[]` — each step: `name`, `status`, `conclusion`, `started_at`, `completed_at`

138	- `name`, `app.name` — which tool
139	- `status`, `conclusion`
140	- `started_at`, `completed_at`
141	- `output.annotations_count` — issues found
142	- `output.title`, `.summary`
143	
144	### Commit Statuses (legacy CI)
145	- `state` — error/failure/pending/success
146	- `context` — CI system name
147	- `creator`, `created_at`

151	## Deployments & Environments
152	
153	### Deployments
154	- `sha`, `ref`, `environment`, `task` (deploy/deploy:migrations)
155	- `creator`, `created_at`
156	- `transient_environment`, `production_environment`
157	
158	### Deployment Statuses
159	- `state` — error/failure/pending/in_progress/queued/success
160	- `environment_url`, `log_url`

165	- `deployment_branch_policy`

169	## Security Signals
170	
171	### Code Scanning Alerts
172	- `state` — open/dismissed/fixed
173	- `severity` — critical/high/medium/low/warning/note/error
174	- `rule.id`, `rule.name`, `rule.security_severity_level`, `rule.tags[]`
175	- `tool.name`, `tool.version` (CodeQL, Semgrep, etc.)
176	- `created_at`, `fixed_at`, `dismissed_at`
177	- `dismissed_reason` — false positive / won't fix / used in tests
178	- `dismissed_by`, `dismissal_approved_by`
179	- `most_recent_instance.location` — file path + line/column
180	- `most_recent_instance.classifications` — source/generated/test/library
181	
182	### Secret Scanning Alerts
183	- `secret_type`, `provider`, `validity` — active/inactive/unknown
184	- `push_protection_bypassed` — boolean, **developer bypassed protection**
185	- `push_protection_bypassed_by`, `push_protection_bypassed_at`
186	- `resolution` — false_positive/wont_fix/revoked/used_in_tests
187	- `publicly_leaked`, `multi_repo`

190	- `severity` — low/medium/high/critical
191	- `package.ecosystem`, `package.name`, `vulnerable_version_range`

193	- `dismissed_reason` — fix_started/inaccurate/no_bandwidth/not_used/tolerable_risk

197	### Dependency Review (per PR)
198	Per changed dependency: `change_type` (added/removed), `ecosystem`, `name`, `version`, `vulnerabilities[]` with severity + GHSA/CVE IDs

251	## Webhooks (Real-Time Events)
252	
253	Subscribe instead of polling. Key events for performance tracking:
254	- `push` — commits with file changes
255	- `pull_request` — all lifecycle (opened/closed/merged/draft/ready_for_review/review_requested)
256	- `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `pull_request_review_thread`

266	## Rate Limits
267	
268	| Auth Type | REST/hr | GraphQL points/hr |
269	|-----------|---------|-------------------|
270	| GitHub App installation | 5,000–12,500 (scales) | 5,000 |
271	| Personal access token | 5,000 | 5,000 |
272	| Enterprise Cloud | 15,000 | 10,000 |
273	
274	**Key rules:**
275	- 100 concurrent requests max
276	- 900 REST points/minute
277	- Stats endpoints: async computed, return 202 until ready — cache aggressively
278	- `If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since` — 304 responses don't count against limit
279	- Commit stats (additions/deletions) need one call per commit — batch via GraphQL
```

```
1	import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';
2	
3	import { InjectQueue } from '@nestjs/bullmq';
4	import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
5	import { Queue } from 'bullmq';
6	
7	import { EnvConfigService } from '@modules/env-config/env-config.service';
8	import { GithubInstallationModel } from '@modules/github/db/github-installations.model';
9	import { IGithubInstallationEvent } from '@modules/github/types/github-api.interface';
10	import { GithubInstallationStatus } from '@modules/github/types/github-installation.interface';
11	
12	import { GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET } from '@constants/env-variables.constant';
13	
14	@Injectable()
15	export class GithubWebhookService {
16		private readonly logger = new Logger(GithubWebhookService.name);
17	
18		constructor(
19			private readonly configService: EnvConfigService,
20			private readonly githubInstallationModel: GithubInstallationModel,
21			@InjectQueue('github') private readonly githubQueue: Queue,
22		) {}
23	
24		verifySignature({
25			payload,
26			signature,
27		}: {
28			payload: string;
29			signature: string;
30		}): boolean {
31			const secret = this.configService.get<string>({ key: GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET });
32			const computed = `sha256=${createHmac('sha256', secret).update(payload).digest('hex')}`;
33	
34			const trusted = Buffer.from(signature);
35			const untrusted = Buffer.from(computed);
36	
37			if (trusted.length !== untrusted.length) return false;
38			return timingSafeEqual(trusted, untrusted);
39		}
40	
41		async handleEvent({
42			event,
43			installationId,
44			payload,
45		}: {
46			event: string;
47			installationId: number;
48			payload: unknown;
49		}): Promise<void> {
50			const installation = await this.githubInstallationModel.findByInstallationId({
51				installationId,
52			});
53	
54			if (!installation) {
55				this.logger.warn(`Webhook received for unknown installation: ${installationId}`);
56				return;
57			}
58	
59			if (installation.status === GithubInstallationStatus.UNINSTALLED) {
60				this.logger.warn(
61					`Webhook received for uninstalled installation: ${installationId}`,
62				);
63				return;
64			}
65	
66			if (event === 'installation') {
67				await this.handleInstallationLifecycle({
68					installationId,
69					payload: payload as IGithubInstallationEvent,
70				});
71				return;
72			}
73	
74			if (installation.status === GithubInstallationStatus.SUSPENDED) {
75				this.logger.warn(`Dropping event for suspended installation: ${installationId}`);
76				return;
77			}
78	
79			await this.githubQueue.add('raw_event', {
80				event,
81				installationId,
82				payload,
83				receivedAt: new Date(),
84			});
85	
86			this.logger.debug(`Queued ${event} event for installation ${installationId}`);
87		}
88	
89		private async handleInstallationLifecycle({
90			installationId,
91			payload,
92		}: {
93			installationId: number;
94			payload: IGithubInstallationEvent;
95		}): Promise<void> {
96			if (payload.action === 'deleted') {
97				await this.githubInstallationModel.markUninstalled({ installationId });
98				this.logger.debug(`Installation ${installationId} uninstalled`);
99			} else if (payload.action === 'suspend') {
100				await this.githubInstallationModel.markSuspended({ installationId });
101				this.logger.debug(`Installation ${installationId} suspended`);
102			} else if (payload.action === 'unsuspend') {
103				await this.githubInstallationModel.markActive({ installationId });
104				this.logger.debug(`Installation ${installationId} unsuspended`);
105			}
106		}
107	}
108	
```

```
30		generateAppJwt(): string {
31			const appId = this.configService.get<string>({ key: GITHUB_APP_ID });
32			const rawKey = this.configService.get<string>({ key: GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY });
33			const privateKey = rawKey.replace(/\\n/g, '\n');
34	
35			const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
36			const header = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ alg: 'RS256', typ: 'JWT' })).toString(
37				'base64url',
38			);
39			const payload = Buffer.from(
40				JSON.stringify({ iat: now - 60, exp: now + 600, iss: appId }),
41			).toString('base64url');
42			const data = `${header}.${payload}`;
43	
44			const sign = createSign('RSA-SHA256');
45			sign.update(data);
46			const signature = sign.sign(privateKey, 'base64url');
47	
48			return `${data}.${signature}`;
49		}
50	
51		async getInstallationToken({
52			installationId,
53		}: {
54			installationId: number;
55		}): Promise<string> {
56			const cached = await this.cacheService.get<string>({
57				namespace: Namespaces.GITHUB_TOKEN,
58				key: String(installationId),
59				consistencyLevel: ConsistencyLevel.STRONG,
60			});
61	
62			if (cached) {
63				return cached;
64			}
65	
66			const jwt = this.generateAppJwt();
67			const { data } = await this.httpService.axiosRef.post<IGithubApiInstallationToken>(
68				`https://api.github.com/app/installations/${installationId}/access_tokens`,
69				{},
70				{
71					headers: {
72						Authorization: `Bearer ${jwt}`,
73						Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
74						'X-GitHub-Api-Version': '2022-11-28',
75					},
76				},
77			);
78	
79			await this.cacheService.set({
80				namespace: Namespaces.GITHUB_TOKEN,
81				key: String(installationId),
82				value: data.token,
83				ttl: GITHUB_TOKEN_TTL_MS,
84			});
85	
86			this.logger.debug(`Generated installation token for installation ${installationId}`);
87			return data.token;
```

> AGENT

Here's the full picture:

---

## Current state

The plumbing is done:
- Webhook arrives → signature verified → `handleInstallationLifecycle` **or** pushed to BullMQ `raw_event` job
- `GithubAppService` can authenticate, get tokens, list repos
- Install flow creates `github_installations` + syncs `github_repos`

**The queue has no consumer.** Events are being queued but nothing processes them.

---

## What needs to be built

### 1. BullMQ processor (`github-event.processor.ts`)
The missing piece. A `@Processor('github')` that dequeues `raw_event` jobs and routes by event type:

| Event | Data to store |
|---|---|
| `push` | commits → `github_commits` table |
| `pull_request` | PR lifecycle → `github_pull_requests` table |
| `pull_request_review` | review state → `github_reviews` table |
| `pull_request_review_comment` | inline comments → `github_review_comments` table |

### 2. New DB tables + models
Need migrations + models for:
- `github_commits` — sha, message, author_login, committed_at, additions, deletions, repo_id
- `github_pull_requests` — pr number, title, state, author, created_at, merged_at, cycle_time
- `github_reviews` — state (APPROVED/CHANGES_REQUESTED/etc), submitted_at, reviewer, pr_id
- `github_review_comments` — body, path, line, created_at, pr_id

### 3. Historical backfill (polling)
After install callback → `syncRepos()` already fires. Need a parallel `backfillHistory()` that:
1. Enqueues a BullMQ `backfill` job per repo
2. Processor paginates GitHub REST API: all commits, all PRs, reviews per PR
3. Idempotent upserts (don't double-store on re-run)

### 4. Contributor identity mapping
When any event arrives with a GitHub user, upsert into `github_contributors`:
```
github_login, github_user_id, company_id, platform_user_id (nullable)
```
`platform_user_id` stays `null` until admin manually maps them via UI (Phase 4 concern).

---

## What you need to provide

**Code — nothing, I can build all of this.**

**Infrastructure — you need:**

1. **A GitHub App** (if not already created):
   - Go to `github.com/settings/apps` → New GitHub App
   - Set webhook URL (needs to be a public URL)
   - Generate a private key (RSA `.pem` file)
   - Note: App ID, Client ID, webhook secret
   - Permissions needed: `Contents: read`, `Pull requests: read`, `Checks: read`, `Metadata: read`
   - Subscribe to events: `push`, `pull_request`, `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`

2. **Public webhook URL** for local dev:
   - Use `ngrok http 3000` (or whatever port your backend runs on)
   - Set that as webhook URL in GitHub App settings

3. **Env vars** (already partially wired, just need real values):
   ```
   GITHUB_APP_ID=...
   GITHUB_APP_NAME=...
   GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY=...  (paste the .pem contents, \n-escaped)
   GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET=...
   ```

---

Do you already have a GitHub App created, or should I start building the processor + DB layer now?

> DEVELOPER

ok a few question first...
company registered and instaled GH app.. they synced historical data, how will we updated their stats duting operations?
by crone? by hooks? how?

> AGENT

**Webhooks are the primary mechanism — they're already built.**

Here's how it works operationally:

---

## Normal operations flow

```
Developer pushes code / opens PR / submits review
        ↓
GitHub fires webhook → your /webhook endpoint
        ↓
Signature verified → queued to BullMQ
        ↓
Processor stores to DB (real-time, sub-second)
```

No cron needed for day-to-day. Webhooks handle everything live.

---

## The gap: webhooks can fail

GitHub retries failed webhooks ~3x over ~1hr, then **gives up**. If your server was down, you lose events.

So you need a **reconciliation cron** — not a full re-sync, just gap-filling:

```
Every hour (or daily):
  For each active installation:
    Poll GitHub: "give me activity since last_synced_at"
    Upsert anything missing (idempotent)
    Update last_synced_at
```

This is lightweight — uses `since` param on GitHub API, not a full historical scan.

---

## Summary

| Mechanism | Purpose | Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| **Webhooks** | Real-time updates during normal ops | On every dev action |
| **Backfill job** | Historical data on first install | Once, at install |
| **Reconciliation cron** | Gap-fill for missed webhooks | Hourly or daily |

---

**What you need to decide:** reconciliation frequency. Hourly = tighter data, more API calls. Daily = good enough for analytics, minimal cost.

My recommendation: **daily cron**. This is analytics data, not a live dashboard — 24hr staleness is acceptable and keeps you well within GitHub's rate limits even at scale.

> DEVELOPER

ok ... imagine company has 400 devs.. how many events per day we might handle? imagine we will have 30 comanies...will we be able to handle it in terms of GH quota?

> AGENT

Good question. Let me break it down properly.

---

## Webhook volume (no rate limit — GitHub pushes to us)

**Per company, 400 devs, ~70% active daily:**

| Event type | Estimate/day |
|---|---|
| Push events | ~500 (batched, ~3 commits each) |
| PR events (open/update/merge) | ~600 |
| Review events | ~200 |
| Review comments | ~400 |
| **Total per company** | **~1,700/day** |

**30 companies → ~51,000 webhook events/day → ~35/min**

BullMQ handles thousands per second. **Zero concern here.**

---

## GitHub API rate limits (the real question)

**Critical insight: each company = its own installation token = its own rate limit bucket.**

30 companies don't compete. They're isolated.

Per installation, GitHub scales the limit with org size:
```
base 5,000 + (50 × members) + (30 × repos), max 12,500/hr
400 devs × 50 = 20,000 → capped at 12,500/hr
```

So each company gets **12,500 req/hr = 300,000 req/day**.

---

## Where those requests get consumed

### Reconciliation cron (daily, per company)
```
50 repos × (commits since yesterday + PRs updated) ≈ 100-200 calls/day
```
**Negligible. 0.07% of daily quota.**

### Historical backfill (one-time per company)
This is where it gets real:
```
50 repos × 2yr history:
  - Commits: ~1,000 calls/repo (100/page)
  - PRs: ~500 calls/repo
  - Reviews per PR: ~200 calls/repo
Total: ~85,000 API calls per company
```

At 12,500/hr limit → **~7 hours per company backfill.**

But since each company is isolated → all 30 can backfill in parallel. **No contention.**

---

## Risk areas

**1. Backfill speed** — 7hrs is fine for onboarding but you need a **rate limiter in the BullMQ processor** (e.g., BullMQ's built-in `limiter: { max: 100, duration: 1000 }` per installation). Without it you'll hit 429s.

**2. Stats endpoints** — `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/stats/contributors` returns 202 while computing, then 200. These are expensive + cached by GitHub. Don't poll these — use raw event data instead.

**3. DB write volume** — 30 companies backfilling simultaneously = potentially millions of rows being written. Need proper indexing from day 1 (`repo_id`, `author_login`, `committed_at`).

---

## Bottom line

You're **fine at 30 companies / 400 devs each.** The architecture scales well past that because rate limits are per-installation, not global.

The only thing to implement carefully: **rate-limited BullMQ queues per installation during backfill.**

> DEVELOPER

ok... which approach better, cron that updates stats daily for each comapny, or webhook?

> AGENT

Neither alone. The right answer is **both, doing different jobs.**

The key distinction you need to make:

---

## Two separate concerns

### Raw data ingestion → **Webhooks** (already built)
GitHub pushes events → we store commits, PRs, reviews into DB in real-time.
No choice here — this must be webhook-driven.

### Stats calculation → **Cron** (reads your own DB, not GitHub)
Every night: read raw events from your DB → compute metrics → write to stats tables.

```
Cron → reads github_commits, github_pull_requests, github_reviews
     → calculates PR cycle time, commit frequency, review response time, etc.
     → writes to developer_stats, team_stats tables
     → dashboard reads from stats tables
```

**No GitHub API calls involved.** You're aggregating your own data.

---

## Why not webhook-driven stats?

If you update stats on every incoming event:
- PR merged → update cycle time ✓
- But what if a webhook was missed? Stats are silently wrong.
- Formula changes → need to re-run everything anyway
- Race conditions on concurrent updates for same developer

**Cron recalculates from raw truth every time. Missed webhook? Fixed on next run. Formula bug? Re-run cron. Always consistent.**

---

## The architecture

```
GitHub → webhooks → raw event tables  (real-time, webhook-driven)
                         ↓
                    daily cron         (reads raw tables, no GitHub API)
                         ↓
                    stats tables       (what dashboards query)
```

---

**Verdict:** Webhooks for ingestion. Cron for stats. Daily frequency is fine for an analytics product — nobody needs live commit frequency to the second.

> DEVELOPER

what do you mean by GitHub pushes events → we store commits, PRs, reviews into DB in real-time.  

will we store real code, data?

> AGENT

No, not the actual code. **Metadata only.**

---

## What a `push` webhook gives you

```json
{
  "commits": [
    {
      "id": "abc123",
      "message": "fix: null check on user service",
      "author": { "name": "John", "email": "john@co.com" },
      "timestamp": "2026-04-16T10:30:00Z",
      "added": ["src/user.ts"],
      "removed": [],
      "modified": ["src/auth.ts", "src/user.service.ts"]
    }
  ],
  "repository": { "id": 123, "name": "my-repo" }
}
```

**No code. No diffs. No file contents.**

To get `additions`/`deletions` counts you'd need a separate API call per commit (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}`).

---

## What we actually store

| Table | What's stored |
|---|---|
| `github_commits` | sha, message, author login, timestamp, file names touched |
| `github_pull_requests` | title, state, opened_at, merged_at, additions, deletions count |
| `github_reviews` | reviewer, state (APPROVED/CHANGES_REQUESTED), submitted_at |
| `github_review_comments` | comment body, file path, line number, created_at |

**Numbers and timestamps, not code.**

---

## Then stats cron computes from that

```
cycle_time = merged_at - created_at
commit_frequency = count(commits) per week per developer
review_response_time = first_review.submitted_at - pr.created_at
```

Pure math on metadata. No code ever stored.

> DEVELOPER

ok question: we will need to have how many lines of codes per PR, day, year were written, deleted.. etc.. will we have it?

> AGENT

**Partially — depends on granularity.**

---

## Per PR → YES, free from webhook

The `pull_request` event payload includes:
```json
{
  "pull_request": {
    "additions": 142,
    "deletions": 38,
    "changed_files": 5
  }
}
```
Store it. Done.

---

## Per commit → expensive

Push webhook gives you the commit list but **no line counts**. To get them you need one extra API call per commit:
```
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}
→ stats.additions, stats.deletions
```

400 devs × 5 commits/day = 2,000 extra API calls/day per company. Eats quota fast. **Probably not worth it.**

---

## Per week/year → GitHub stats API (best option)

```
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/stats/contributors
```
Returns per contributor, per week, for **52 weeks**: `additions`, `deletions`, `commits`. One call per repo. This is what you want for yearly/weekly trend charts.

**Limitation:** only 52 weeks history, and it's async (returns 202 while computing — need retry logic).

---

## What you'll realistically have

| Granularity | Source | Available |
|---|---|---|
| Per PR | Webhook payload | ✅ Real-time |
| Per week (52wk) | `/stats/contributors` | ✅ On backfill |
| Per day | Approximated from PR merge dates | ⚠️ Approximate |
| Per commit | Extra API call per commit | ❌ Too expensive |

---

**Recommendation:** track lines at PR level (webhook) + weekly rollups (stats API). That's enough for every meaningful metric in your catalog — cycle time, churn, velocity trends.

> DEVELOPER

ok ...when I create this app.. will it be just for dev purposes and later i will need to create the same for prod?

> AGENT

Yes. You'll need **separate apps per environment.**

---

## Why

GitHub App = a registered entity on GitHub with its own:
- App ID
- Private key
- Webhook URL (hardcoded)

You can't point one app at both `localhost` and `prod.yourdomain.com`.

---

## Typical setup

| App name | Webhook URL | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `myapp-dev` | ngrok / local tunnel | Local development |
| `myapp-staging` | `https://staging.yourdomain.com` | Staging env |
| `myapp` | `https://yourdomain.com` | Production |

Each gets its own App ID, private key, webhook secret → own `.env` per environment.

---

## What stays the same

- Permissions (same across all)
- Subscribed events (same across all)
- Your code (env vars swap, nothing else changes)

---

## For now

Just create `myapp-dev`. Keep it simple, install it on your own personal test repo or a throwaway org.

When you're ready for prod, create `myapp` with the real domain — 10 min job, same steps.

> DEVELOPER

ok, my companies, how they will instal this app? just by linK? or they will need to hastle with app creation as well?

> AGENT

**Just a link. Zero hassle for them.**

---

## How it works

YOU own the GitHub App. Your customers just **install** it on their GitHub org.

The flow you already built handles this:

```
Company admin clicks "Connect GitHub" in your app
        ↓
GithubInstallService.initiateConnect() → redirects to:
https://github.com/apps/myapp/installations/new?state=xyz
        ↓
GitHub shows permission screen to company admin
        ↓
Admin clicks "Install" → selects which repos to grant access
        ↓
GitHub redirects back to your callback URL
        ↓
GithubInstallService.handleCallback() → saves installation
```

---

## What the company admin sees

Just GitHub's standard permission screen:

```
"MyApp" wants access to your organization
- Read access to code
- Read access to pull requests
- Read access to metadata

[Install] [Cancel]
```

One click. Done. No App ID, no keys, no config.

---

## They never touch GitHub App settings

That's your infrastructure. They just grant permission like installing any other GitHub integration (Vercel, Linear, Slack, etc.).

The list I gave you is incomplete. Here's the full correct set:

---

## Repository permissions

| Permission | Why |
|---|---|
| **Metadata** | Required by GitHub for all apps. Repo info, list repos. |
| **Contents** | Commits, commit stats, `/stats/contributors` (lines/week), punch card |
| **Pull requests** | PRs, reviews, approvals, inline comments, review threads |
| **Checks** | CI check runs (Codecov, SonarQube, etc.) |
| **Actions** | GitHub Actions workflow runs, job durations, success/failure rates |
| **Commit statuses** | Legacy CI (CircleCI, Travis, etc.) |

## Organization permissions

| Permission | Why |
|---|---|
| **Members** | List org members → contributor identity mapping (GitHub user → your platform user) |

---

## Subscribe to events

| Event | Why |
|---|---|
| `push` | Commits |
| `pull_request` | PR lifecycle |
| `pull_request_review` | Approvals, change requests |
| `pull_request_review_comment` | Inline comments |
| `workflow_run` | CI results |
| `check_run` | External CI integrations |
| `member` | Org membership changes |

---

All permissions: **Read-only**. You never need write access.

Push 
Git push to a repository.
Release 
Release created, edited, published, unpublished, or deleted.
Repository

When a message is dispatched from a repository.

Star

> AGENT

Two problems with manually hitting that URL:

1. Route is `GET /api/integrations/github/callback` (has `/api` prefix)
2. Requires auth + `state` param — can't just hit it directly

**The proper flow:**
1. Login to your platform as admin
2. `POST /api/integrations/github/connect` → returns install URL with state
3. Go to that URL → GitHub redirects back with state → saved to DB

Since the app is already installed on GitHub (installation_id `124300964`), you need to either:
- Go through the proper flow via Swagger UI once server is running
- Or uninstall + reinstall after server is up so the callback lands properly

**Complete Example - Github Installations Table:**

```typescript
import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common';

import { TABLE_NAME_GITHUB_INSTALLATIONS } from '@constants/db.constant';

import type { Knex } from 'knex';

const logger = new Logger('20260414120000_create_github_installations_table.ts');

export async function up(knex: Knex): Promise<void> {
	logger.log('Creating github_installations table');

	await knex.transaction(async (trx) => {
		const tableExists = await trx.schema.hasTable(TABLE_NAME_GITHUB_INSTALLATIONS);

		if (!tableExists) {
			await trx.schema.createTable(TABLE_NAME_GITHUB_INSTALLATIONS, (table) => {
				table.uuid('_id').primary().notNullable();
				table.uuid('company_id').notNullable().references('_id').inTable('companies');
				table.bigInteger('installation_id').notNullable().unique();
				table.string('org_login', 255).notNullable();
				table.bigInteger('org_id').notNullable();
				table
					.enum('status', ['active', 'suspended', 'uninstalled'])
					.notNullable()
					.defaultTo('active');
				table.timestamp('installed_at', { useTz: true }).notNullable();
				table.timestamp('suspended_at', { useTz: true }).nullable();
				table.timestamp('uninstalled_at', { useTz: true }).nullable();
				table
					.timestamp('created_at', { useTz: true })
					.defaultTo(trx.fn.now())
					.notNullable();
				table
					.timestamp('updated_at', { useTz: true })
					.defaultTo(trx.fn.now())
					.notNullable();

				table.index(['company_id']);
			});

			logger.log('Successfully created github_installations table');
		} else {
			logger.log('github_installations table already exists, skipping');
		}
	});
}

export async function down(knex: Knex): Promise<void> {
	logger.log('Dropping github_installations table');

	await knex.transaction(async (trx) => {
		await trx.schema.dropTableIfExists(TABLE_NAME_GITHUB_INSTALLATIONS);
	});
}
```

### 3. Existing Model Patterns

**File:** `/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/no-name-proj/backend/src/modules/github/db/github-repos.model.ts`

```typescript
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Knex } from 'knex';
import { InjectConnection } from 'nest-knexjs';

import { KNEX_READ_CONNECTION, KNEX_WRITE_CONNECTION } from '@modules/db/db.constant';
import { IGithubApiRepo } from '@modules/github/types/github-api.interface';
import { IGithubRepoBase } from '@modules/github/types/github-repo.interface';

import { TABLE_NAME_GITHUB_REPOS } from '@constants/db.constant';

@Injectable()
export class GithubRepoModel {
	private readonly logger = new Logger(GithubRepoModel.name);
	private readonly tableName = TABLE_NAME_GITHUB_REPOS;

	constructor(
		@InjectConnection(KNEX_READ_CONNECTION) private readonly knexRead: Knex,
		@InjectConnection(KNEX_WRITE_CONNECTION) private readonly knexWrite: Knex,
	) {}

	async upsertMany({
		installationId,
		repos,
	}: {
		installationId: string;
		repos: IGithubApiRepo[];
	}): Promise<void> {
		if (repos.length === 0) return;

		try {
			const rows = repos.map((repo) => ({
				_id: randomUUID(),
				installation_id: installationId,
				github_repo_id: repo.id,
				name: repo.name,
				full_name: repo.full_name,
				private: repo.private,
				default_branch: repo.default_branch,
				created_at: this.knexWrite.fn.now(),
				updated_at: this.knexWrite.fn.now(),
			}));

			await this.knexWrite<IGithubRepoBase>(this.tableName)
				.insert(rows)
				.onConflict('github_repo_id')
				.merge([
					'installation_id',
					'name',
					'full_name',
					'private',
					'default_branch',
					'updated_at',
				]);

			this.logger.debug(
				`Upserted ${repos.length} repos for installation ${installationId}`,
			);
		} catch (error) {
			this.logger.error(
				`Failed to upsert repos for installation ${installationId}: ${(error as Error).message}`,
			);
			throw error;
		}
	}

	async findByInstallationId({
		installationId,
	}: {
		installationId: string;
	}): Promise<IGithubRepoBase[]> {
		try {
			return await this.knexRead<IGithubRepoBase>(this.tableName)
				.where({ installation_id: installationId })
				.select('*');
		} catch (error) {
			this.logger.error(
				`Failed to find repos for installation ${installationId}: ${(error as Error).message}`,
			);
			throw error;
		}
	}

	async removeByGithubIds({
		installationId,
		githubRepoIds,
	}: {
		installationId: string;
		githubRepoIds: number[];
	}): Promise<void> {
		if (githubRepoIds.length === 0) return;

		try {
			await this.knexWrite<IGithubRepoBase>(this.tableName)
				.where({ installation_id: installationId })
				.whereIn('github_repo_id', githubRepoIds)
				.delete();

			this.logger.debug(
				`Removed ${githubRepoIds.length} repos from installation ${installationId}`,
			);
		} catch (error) {
			this.logger.error(
				`Failed to remove repos from installation ${installationId}: ${(error as Error).message}`,
			);
			throw error;
		}
	}
}
```

```typescript
import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Test, TestingModule } from '@nestjs/testing';

import { KNEX_READ_CONNECTION, KNEX_WRITE_CONNECTION } from '@modules/db/db.constant';
import { GithubRepoModel } from '@modules/github/db/github-repos.model';
import { IGithubApiRepo } from '@modules/github/types/github-api.interface';
import { IGithubRepoBase } from '@modules/github/types/github-repo.interface';

const mockRepo: IGithubRepoBase = {
	_id: 'repo-uuid-1',
	installation_id: 'install-uuid-1',
	github_repo_id: 111222333,
	name: 'api',
	full_name: 'acme-corp/api',
	private: true,
	default_branch: 'main',
	synced_at: null,
	created_at: new Date('2026-04-14'),
	updated_at: new Date('2026-04-14'),
};

const mockKnexRead = {
	where: jest.fn().mockReturnThis(),
	select: jest.fn(),
};
const mockKnexWrite = {
	insert: jest.fn().mockReturnThis(),
	where: jest.fn().mockReturnThis(),
	whereIn: jest.fn().mockReturnThis(),
	delete: jest.fn(),
	onConflict: jest.fn().mockReturnThis(),
	merge: jest.fn(),
};

const knexReadFn = jest.fn().mockReturnValue(mockKnexRead);
const knexWriteFn = jest.fn().mockReturnValue(mockKnexWrite);

(knexWriteFn as jest.Mock & { fn: { now: jest.Mock } }).fn = {
	now: jest.fn().mockReturnValue('NOW()'),
};

describe('GithubRepoModel', () => {
	let model: GithubRepoModel;

	beforeEach(async () => {
		jest.clearAllMocks();

		knexReadFn.mockReturnValue(mockKnexRead);
		knexWriteFn.mockReturnValue(mockKnexWrite);
		mockKnexRead.where.mockReturnThis();
		mockKnexWrite.insert.mockReturnThis();
		mockKnexWrite.where.mockReturnThis();
		mockKnexWrite.whereIn.mockReturnThis();
		mockKnexWrite.onConflict.mockReturnThis();

		const module: TestingModule = await Test.createTestingModule({
			providers: [
				GithubRepoModel,
				{ provide: KNEX_READ_CONNECTION, useValue: knexReadFn },
				{ provide: KNEX_WRITE_CONNECTION, useValue: knexWriteFn },
			],
		}).compile();

		model = module.get<GithubRepoModel>(GithubRepoModel);

		jest.spyOn(Logger.prototype, 'log').mockImplementation(jest.fn());
		jest.spyOn(Logger.prototype, 'error').mockImplementation(jest.fn());
		jest.spyOn(Logger.prototype, 'debug').mockImplementation(jest.fn());
	});

	afterEach(() => jest.clearAllMocks());

	it('should be defined', () => {
		expect(model).toBeDefined();
	});

	describe('upsertMany', () => {
		it('should do nothing when repos array is empty', async () => {
			await model.upsertMany({ installationId: 'install-uuid-1', repos: [] });
			expect(knexWriteFn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
		});

		it('should insert repos with onConflict merge', async () => {
			mockKnexWrite.merge = jest.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined);
			const repos: IGithubApiRepo[] = [
				{
					id: mockRepo.github_repo_id,
					name: mockRepo.name,
					full_name: mockRepo.full_name,
					private: mockRepo.private,
					default_branch: mockRepo.default_branch,
				},
			];

			await model.upsertMany({ installationId: 'install-uuid-1', repos });

			expect(knexWriteFn).toHaveBeenCalled();
			expect(mockKnexWrite.onConflict).toHaveBeenCalledWith('github_repo_id');
			expect(mockKnexWrite.merge).toHaveBeenCalled();
		});

		it('should throw when DB throws', async () => {
			mockKnexWrite.merge = jest.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('DB error'));
			const repos: IGithubApiRepo[] = [
				{
					id: mockRepo.github_repo_id,
					name: mockRepo.name,
					full_name: mockRepo.full_name,
					private: mockRepo.private,
					default_branch: mockRepo.default_branch,
				},
			];

			await expect(
				model.upsertMany({ installationId: 'install-uuid-1', repos }),
			).rejects.toThrow('DB error');
		});
	});

	describe('findByInstallationId', () => {
		it('should return repos for the installation', async () => {
			mockKnexRead.select = jest.fn().mockResolvedValue([mockRepo]);

			const result = await model.findByInstallationId({
				installationId: mockRepo.installation_id,
			});

			expect(result).toEqual([mockRepo]);
		});

		it('should throw when DB throws', async () => {
			mockKnexRead.select = jest.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('DB read error'));

			await expect(
				model.findByInstallationId({ installationId: mockRepo.installation_id }),
			).rejects.toThrow('DB read error');
		});
	});

	describe('removeByGithubIds', () => {
		it('should do nothing when githubRepoIds is empty', async () => {
			await model.removeByGithubIds({
				installationId: mockRepo.installation_id,
				githubRepoIds: [],
			});
			expect(knexWriteFn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
		});

		it('should delete repos with matching github ids', async () => {
			mockKnexWrite.delete = jest.fn().mockResolvedValue(1);

			await model.removeByGithubIds({
				installationId: mockRepo.installation_id,
				githubRepoIds: [mockRepo.github_repo_id],
			});

			expect(mockKnexWrite.whereIn).toHaveBeenCalledWith('github_repo_id', [
				mockRepo.github_repo_id,
			]);
			expect(mockKnexWrite.delete).toHaveBeenCalled();
		});

		it('should throw when DB throws', async () => {
			mockKnexWrite.delete = jest.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('DB delete error'));

			await expect(
				model.removeByGithubIds({
					installationId: mockRepo.installation_id,
					githubRepoIds: [mockRepo.github_repo_id],
				}),
			).rejects.toThrow('DB delete error');
		});
	});
});
```

```typescript
import { KNEX_READ_CONNECTION, KNEX_WRITE_CONNECTION } from '@modules/db/db.constant';

describe('DbModule (e2e)', () => {

		it('should have all expected tables after migration', async () => {
			const tables = await knexWrite
				.select('tablename')
				.from('pg_tables')
				.where({ schemaname: 'public' })
				.whereNotIn('tablename', ['knex_migrations', 'knex_migrations_lock']);

			const tableNames = tables.map((t: { tablename: string }) => t.tablename);

			expect(tableNames).toEqual(
				expect.arrayContaining([
					'users',
					'companies',
					'company_members',
					'oauth_accounts',
					'invitations',
				]),
			);
		});
	});
});
```

## Key Architectural Patterns Summary

**Database Layer:**
- Read/Write connection separation via Knex with connection pooling (min 2, max 10)
- Models use single object parameter destructuring (enforced ESLint rule)
- Prepared statements with type safety via interfaces
- UUID primary keys with Knex transaction support

**Migration Pattern:**
- Timestamp-based naming with idempotency checks (table existence validation)
- Single transaction per migration with Logger
- Table name constants imported from `@constants/db.constant`
- Always includes `up()` and `down()` functions

**Testing Pattern:**
- Unit tests mock all external dependencies (Knex connections)
- E2E tests import full AppModule with real database connections
- Logger spies prevent console noise during tests
- Models are injected via TestingModule

**Module Pattern:**
- Global DbModule exports KnexModule with read/write connections
- Services injectable with `@InjectConnection()` decorator
- Constants-driven configuration via env-variables

All files are located at:
- Migrations: `/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/no-name-proj/backend/src/migrations/`
- Models: `/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/no-name-proj/backend/src/modules/github/db/`
- Types: `/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/no-name-proj/backend/src/modules/github/types/`
- Constants: `/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/no-name-proj/backend/src/constants/`
- Tests: `/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/no-name-proj/backend/src/unit-tests/` and `/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/no-name-proj/backend/test/`

```
1	# GitHub App Integration Implementation Plan
2	
3	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

5	**Goal:** Allow company admins to connect their GitHub organization(s) via GitHub App installation, with persistent API access and real-time webhook ingestion.
6	
7	**Architecture:** Admin initiates install via a state-protected redirect to GitHub, which calls back to our endpoint after org install. We store the installation and repo list in Postgres, generate short-lived installation tokens (cached in Redis, generated server-side from our private key), and route webhook events to a BullMQ queue for async processing.
```

> AGENT

Found it. The read replica (port 5433) has replication lag - the test inserts a user to the write DB (port 5432), then the app reads from port 5433 which hasn't replicated the user yet.

Fix: point `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` in `.env.test` to the write DB to eliminate replication lag in tests.

All done. Summary of what was fixed in this session:

**Root cause of 41 failing e2e tests**: tests were run without `--runInBand`, causing parallel execution with DB conflicts. The actual `npm run test:e2e` uses `--runInBand` correctly.

**Root cause of the 1 pre-existing e2e failure** (Google OAuth linking token test): streaming PostgreSQL read replica on port 5433 had replication lag — test wrote user to write DB (5432), app read from replica (5433) before data replicated. Fixed by pointing `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` to the write DB (5432) in `.env.test`.

**Lint errors fixed**: `require()` → ES import in `github-webhook.service.unit-spec.ts`, `async () =>` without `await` in `cache.module.e2e-spec.ts`.

**Final state**:
- Unit: 724/724 tests, 99.25% statement coverage
- E2E: 150/150 tests, 97.59% statement coverage
- All thresholds ≥ 95% — CI green
